newsitem.title: THAILAND: FORECAST-Siam Cement '97 profit seen flat.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Siam Cement '97 profit seen flat.

text.p: Profits of Thailand's largest industrial conglomerate, Siam Cement Plc, are seen slowing in 1997 as a flagging economy and cement oversupply hit earnings, analysts said on Monday.
"For 1997, I expect it's not going to be very strong (for Siam Cement) and (profit growth) is expected to be about flat," Eric Uchida Henderson, investment analyst at ING Baring, told Reuters.
Analysts had forecast that Siam Cement would post a consolidated profit of 7.0-7.1 billion baht ($269-$273 million) in 1996 against 6.06 billion baht in the previous year.
Siam Cement is expected to formally announce its 1996 earning results early next month.

"It will be quite tough for the company this year. I forecast the company's (earning) growth to be at only five percent," Visit Ongpipattanakul, senior investment analyst at HSBC James Capel Asia, told Reuters.
The anticipated slowing of Siam Cement's profit this year has prompted investors, especially foreigners, to sell off the shares recently, analysts said.
Siam Cement shares tumbled to a 39-month low at the close on Thursday at 728 baht.
Analysts said the slowing economy would reduce demand for building materials and cement which had been faced with an oversupply from more newly-completed cement plants.
"The economy will play a factor and also cement business will be very difficult (this year)," Henderson said.
The Bank of Thailand projects gross domestic product will grow at 7.1 percent this year compared with 6.7 in 1996.
Henderson said an additional 13.5 million tonnes of cement from new plants would cause the oversupply and overproduction capacity of the cement sector in Thailand.
Siam Cement currently has a cement production capacity of about 20 million tonnes, analysts said.
"The group's paper business may pick up this year on rising world pulp and paper price. But the rise will not be significant," said Visit at HSBC James Capel.
